q: 这是我___书包。
zh: 这是我的书包。
py: zhè shì wǒ de shū bāo
en: This is my school bag.
why: 我 is the owner and 书包 is a noun, so 的 links them. 得 follows a verb or adjective and 地 sits before a verb; neither can join a possessor to a noun.

q: 老师有一本很大___词典。
zh: 老师有一本很大的词典。
py: lǎo shī yǒu yī běn hěn dà de cí diǎn
en: The teacher has a very big dictionary.
why: 很大 describes the noun 词典 that comes next, so the link is 的. 地 would need a verb after it.

q: 她是一个很好___学生。
zh: 她是一个很好的学生。
py: tā shì yī gè hěn hǎo de xué sheng
en: She is a very good student.
why: 好 describes the noun 学生, so 的. 得 would need a verb before it, and 地 a verb after it.

q: 办公室里有一台很旧___打印机。
zh: 办公室里有一台很旧的打印机。
py: bàn gōng shì lǐ yǒu yī tái hěn jiù de dǎ yìn jī
en: There is a very old printer in the office.
why: The word after the gap is the noun 打印机 and 很旧 describes it, so 的. 地 only goes in front of a verb.

q: 经理给了我一份很重要___文件。
zh: 经理给了我一份很重要的文件。
py: jīng lǐ gěi le wǒ yī fèn hěn zhòng yào de wén jiàn
en: The manager gave me a very important document.
why: 很重要 modifies the noun 文件. Adjective + noun is joined with 的; 地 and 得 both need a verb beside them.

q: 我们公司需要一位经验丰富___工程师。
zh: 我们公司需要一位经验丰富的工程师。
py: wǒ men gōng sī xū yào yī wèi jīng yàn fēng fù de gōng chéng shī
en: Our company needs an experienced engineer.
why: 经验丰富 is a descriptive phrase and 工程师 is the noun it describes, so 的. Even a longer phrase before a noun takes 的, never 地.

q: 这是我昨天写___信。
zh: 这是我昨天写的信。
py: zhè shì wǒ zuó tiān xiě de xìn
en: This is the letter I wrote yesterday.
why: The gap follows the verb 写, but what comes next is the noun 信, so the clause 我昨天写 describes it with 的. 得 would need a judgement like 很快 after it.

q: 老师讲___课很有意思。
zh: 老师讲的课很有意思。
py: lǎo shī jiǎng de kè hěn yǒu yì si
en: The lesson the teacher gave is very interesting.
why: 老师讲 is a clause describing the noun 课, so 的. 得 would be followed by a judgement of how well he explained, not by a noun.

q: 这是老师给我___作业。
zh: 这是老师给我的作业。
py: zhè shì lǎo shī gěi wǒ de zuò yè
en: This is the homework the teacher gave me.
why: 老师给我 describes 作业, the noun after the gap, so 的. The verb before the gap does not make it 得 when a noun follows.

q: 坐在前面___那个同学是我朋友。
zh: 坐在前面的那个同学是我朋友。
py: zuò zài qián miàn de nà ge tóng xué shì wǒ péng you
en: The classmate sitting in front is my friend.
why: 坐在前面 is a verb phrase that describes 那个同学, so it takes 的. 得 would need a complement after it, not a noun.

q: 我在网上买___那本字典今天到了。
zh: 我在网上买的那本字典今天到了。
py: wǒ zài wǎng shàng mǎi de nà běn zì diǎn jīn tiān dào le
en: The dictionary I bought online arrived today.
why: 我在网上买 describes the dictionary, so 的 attaches the clause to 那本字典. 买得 would have to be followed by something like 很多.

q: 经理昨天开会说___话，我没听清楚。
zh: 经理昨天开会说的话，我没听清楚。
py: jīng lǐ zuó tiān kāi huì shuō de huà wǒ méi tīng qīng chu
en: I didn't catch clearly what the manager said at the meeting yesterday.
why: 说 + 的 + 话 means 'the words that were said'; the noun 话 after the gap decides for 的. 说得 would be followed by a judgement such as 很快.

q: 他上个星期交给经理___报告，经理还没看完。
zh: 他上个星期交给经理的报告，经理还没看完。
py: tā shàng gè xīng qī jiāo gěi jīng lǐ de bào gào jīng lǐ hái méi kàn wán
en: The report he handed to the manager last week, the manager hasn't finished reading yet.
why: 交给经理 is a verb phrase that describes 报告, so the clause takes 的. 得 and 地 cannot link a verb phrase to a following noun.

q: 在会议上提出这个建议___人是小王。
zh: 在会议上提出这个建议的人是小王。
py: zài huì yì shàng tí chū zhè ge jiàn yì de rén shì xiǎo wáng
en: The person who made this suggestion at the meeting was Xiao Wang.
why: The whole clause 在会议上提出这个建议 describes the noun 人, so 的. The long clause does not change the rule: noun next means 的.

q: 小王跑___很快。
zh: 小王跑得很快。
py: xiǎo wáng pǎo de hěn kuài
en: Xiao Wang runs fast.
why: 很快 judges how he runs and follows the verb 跑 directly, so 得. 的 needs a noun after it and 地 a verb.

q: 他今天来___很早。
zh: 他今天来得很早。
py: tā jīn tiān lái de hěn zǎo
en: He came very early today.
why: 来 + 得 + 很早 judges how early he came, so 得. No 了 is added after 来 here, and no noun follows the gap for 的.

q: 弟弟昨天睡___太晚了。
zh: 弟弟昨天睡得太晚了。
py: dì di zuó tiān shuì de tài wǎn le
en: My younger brother went to bed too late yesterday.
why: 太晚 is a judgement on how he slept, placed after the verb 睡, so 得. 地 would need a verb directly after the gap.

q: 昨天晚上我睡___不太好。
zh: 昨天晚上我睡得不太好。
py: zuó tiān wǎn shang wǒ shuì de bù tài hǎo
en: I didn't sleep very well last night.
why: The negative judgement 不太好 comes after the verb 睡 and is linked with 得. 的 would need a noun and 地 a following verb.

q: 这次考试小李考___特别好。
zh: 这次考试小李考得特别好。
py: zhè cì kǎo shì xiǎo lǐ kǎo de tè bié hǎo
en: Xiao Li did especially well in this exam.
why: 特别好 grades how he took the exam, so it follows 考 with 得. 的 would need a noun after it, and 地 a verb.

q: 同学们都来___很准时。
zh: 同学们都来得很准时。
py: tóng xué men dōu lái de hěn zhǔn shí
en: The students all arrived very punctually.
why: 很准时 comments on how they came and sits right after the verb 来, so 得. No noun or verb follows the gap that could call for 的 or 地.

q: 老板今天笑___特别开心。
zh: 老板今天笑得特别开心。
py: lǎo bǎn jīn tiān xiào de tè bié kāi xīn
en: The boss laughed very happily today.
why: 特别开心 describes the way he laughed and follows the verb 笑, so 得. 地 goes before a verb, not after one.

q: 这个学期的课安排___太紧了，学生们没有时间休息。
zh: 这个学期的课安排得太紧了，学生们没有时间休息。
py: zhè ge xué qī de kè ān pái de tài jǐn le xué sheng men méi yǒu shí jiān xiū xi
en: The classes this term are scheduled too tightly; the students have no time to rest.
why: 太紧了 judges how the classes are scheduled and follows the verb 安排, so 得. A noun would have to follow the gap for 的.

q: 他昨天加班加到很晚，所以今天起___特别晚。
zh: 他昨天加班加到很晚，所以今天起得特别晚。
py: tā zuó tiān jiā bān jiā dào hěn wǎn suǒ yǐ jīn tiān qǐ de tè bié wǎn
en: He worked overtime very late yesterday, so he got up especially late today.
why: 特别晚 is a judgement on when he got up, attached to the verb 起 with 得. 的 and 地 both need a noun or verb after the gap.

q: 我累___不想说话。
zh: 我累得不想说话。
py: wǒ lèi de bù xiǎng shuō huà
en: I'm so tired I don't want to talk.
why: 累 is a state and 不想说话 is its result, so adjective + 得 + result. 地 would make 累 the manner of talking, which makes no sense.

q: 今天热___我不想出门。
zh: 今天热得我不想出门。
py: jīn tiān rè de wǒ bù xiǎng chū mén
en: It's so hot today that I don't want to go out.
why: 热 is a weather state and 我不想出门 is the consequence, so 得. 热 cannot describe the manner of an action, so 地 fails.

q: 他最近忙___没有时间吃饭。
zh: 他最近忙得没有时间吃饭。
py: tā zuì jìn máng de méi yǒu shí jiān chī fàn
en: He has been so busy lately that he has no time to eat.
why: 忙 + 得 + clause means 'so busy that ...'. 没有时间吃饭 is the result, not a manner of doing something, so 地 is wrong.

q: 教室里冷___大家都穿上了外套。
zh: 教室里冷得大家都穿上了外套。
py: jiào shì lǐ lěng de dà jiā dōu chuān shàng le wài tào
en: It was so cold in the classroom that everyone put on their coats.
why: 冷 + 得 + a new clause with its own subject 大家 gives 'so cold that ...'. 的 would need a noun to follow, and 地 a manner.

q: 我饿___一口气吃了三个面包。
zh: 我饿得一口气吃了三个面包。
py: wǒ è de yī kǒu qì chī le sān gè miàn bāo
en: I was so hungry that I ate three rolls in one go.
why: 饿 is the state and eating three rolls is the result, so 得. 饿 cannot be the manner of eating the way 认真 can, so 地 is out.

q: 昨天加班到十二点，我困___一上床就睡着了。
zh: 昨天加班到十二点，我困得一上床就睡着了。
py: zuó tiān jiā bān dào shí èr diǎn wǒ kùn de yī shàng chuáng jiù shuì zháo le
en: I worked overtime until twelve yesterday and was so sleepy that I fell asleep the moment I got into bed.
why: 困 + 得 + result clause: falling asleep at once is the consequence of being sleepy. 地 would mean sleepily doing something, which does not fit the result clause.

q: 这道题难___全班只有两个人做对了。
zh: 这道题难得全班只有两个人做对了。
py: zhè dào tí nán de quán bān zhǐ yǒu liǎng gè rén zuò duì le
en: This question was so hard that only two people in the class got it right.
why: 难 + 得 + clause with its own subject 全班 means 'so hard that ...'. 的 would need a noun right after it, and 难 cannot take 地.

q: 同事们笑___眼泪都流出来了。
zh: 同事们笑得眼泪都流出来了。
py: tóng shì men xiào de yǎn lèi dōu liú chū lái le
en: My colleagues laughed so hard that tears came out.
why: 笑 + 得 + result clause: tears flowing is what the laughing led to. 地 would need a verb right after it, and 眼泪都流出来了 is a result, not an action done in a laughing manner.

q: 他说汉语说___很好。
zh: 他说汉语说得很好。
py: tā shuō hàn yǔ shuō de hěn hǎo
en: He speaks Chinese very well.
why: With an object, the verb is repeated and 得 attaches to the second 说. 的 would need a noun after it and 地 a verb.

q: 她唱歌唱___很好听。
zh: 她唱歌唱得很好听。
py: tā chàng gē chàng de hěn hǎo tīng
en: She sings beautifully.
why: 唱歌 is verb + object, so the verb 唱 is repeated and 得 follows it, then comes the judgement 很好听.

q: 我姐姐做饭做___不错。
zh: 我姐姐做饭做得不错。
py: wǒ jiě jie zuò fàn zuò de bù cuò
en: My older sister cooks quite well.
why: The object 饭 is already said, so 做 is repeated and 得 follows it. The judgement 不错 comes after 得.

q: 我同事写报告写___很快。
zh: 我同事写报告写得很快。
py: wǒ tóng shì xiě bào gào xiě de hěn kuài
en: My colleague writes reports very fast.
why: 写报告 has an object, so 写 comes again before 得: 写报告写得很快. 地 would belong before a verb.

q: 小王打字打___特别快。
zh: 小王打字打得特别快。
py: xiǎo wáng dǎ zì dǎ de tè bié kuài
en: Xiao Wang types especially fast.
why: 打字 is verb + object, so only 打 is repeated before 得. 打字得 would put 得 after the object, which is wrong.

q: 我弟弟游泳游___比我好。
zh: 我弟弟游泳游得比我好。
py: wǒ dì di yóu yǒng yóu de bǐ wǒ hǎo
en: My younger brother swims better than I do.
why: 游泳 is verb + object inside, so 游 is repeated before 得. The comparison 比我好 is the judgement after 得.

q: 李老师讲课讲___生动有趣，学生们都喜欢听。
zh: 李老师讲课讲得生动有趣，学生们都喜欢听。
py: lǐ lǎo shī jiǎng kè jiǎng de shēng dòng yǒu qù xué sheng men dōu xǐ huan tīng
en: Teacher Li's lessons are lively and interesting; the students all love listening.
why: 讲课 has an object, so 讲 is repeated and 得 follows it before the judgement 生动有趣. 的 would need a noun after it.

q: 老师说得很慢，所以我全部听___懂。
zh: 老师说得很慢，所以我全部听得懂。
py: lǎo shī shuō de hěn màn suǒ yǐ wǒ quán bù tīng de dǒng
en: The teacher speaks slowly, so I can understand all of it.
why: 所以 shows that the slow speech makes understanding possible: 听得懂 means 'can understand'. 听不懂 would contradict the reason given.

q: 字太小了，我看___见。
zh: 字太小了，我看不见。
py: zì tài xiǎo le wǒ kàn bù jiàn
en: The characters are too small; I can't see them.
why: 太小了 gives the reason for 'cannot': swap 得 for 不 to get 看不见. 看得见 would say the opposite of what the context implies.

q: 菜太多了，我们三个人吃___完。
zh: 菜太多了，我们三个人吃不完。
py: cài tài duō le wǒ men sān gè rén chī bù wán
en: There's too much food; the three of us can't finish it.
why: 太多了 means the food is more than they can eat, so the negative potential 吃不完. 吃得完 'can finish' contradicts the context.

q: 这本书很便宜，学生都买___起。
zh: 这本书很便宜，学生都买得起。
py: zhè běn shū hěn pián yi xué sheng dōu mǎi de qǐ
en: This book is cheap; students can all afford it.
why: 很便宜 means it is affordable, so the positive form 买得起. 买不起 would say nobody can afford it, which contradicts 很便宜.

q: 题目太难了，我做___出来。
zh: 题目太难了，我做不出来。
py: tí mù tài nán le wǒ zuò bù chū lái
en: The question is too hard; I can't work it out.
why: 太难了 explains why he fails: 做不出来 'cannot work out'. 做得出来 would mean he can, which contradicts the reason.

q: 我坐在第一排，黑板上的字看___清楚。
zh: 我坐在第一排，黑板上的字看得清楚。
py: wǒ zuò zài dì yī pái hēi bǎn shàng de zì kàn de qīng chu
en: I sit in the front row, so I can see the writing on the blackboard clearly.
why: The front row makes seeing easy, so the positive 看得清楚. 看不清楚 would clash with sitting at the front.

q: 资料不多，一个晚上肯定准备___完。
zh: 资料不多，一个晚上肯定准备得完。
py: zī liào bù duō yī gè wǎn shang kěn dìng zhǔn bèi de wán
en: There aren't many materials, so one evening is definitely enough to get them ready.
why: 资料不多 and 肯定 point to 'can manage it': 准备得完. 准备不完 would mean there is too much, the reverse of the first clause.

q: 他说得太快，我一句也听___懂。
zh: 他说得太快，我一句也听不懂。
py: tā shuō de tài kuài wǒ yī jù yě tīng bù dǒng
en: He spoke too fast; I couldn't understand a single sentence.
why: 一句也 requires a negative, so 听不懂. 不 replaces 得 inside the verb and result word; 听得懂 would be positive and clash with 一句也.

q: 同学们高兴___回家了。
zh: 同学们高兴地回家了。
py: tóng xué men gāo xìng de huí jiā le
en: The classmates went home happily.
why: 高兴 describes how they went home, so it sits before the verb 回家 with 地. 得 would need to follow a verb and be followed by a result or judgement.

q: 她认真___听老师讲课。
zh: 她认真地听老师讲课。
py: tā rèn zhēn de tīng lǎo shī jiǎng kè
en: She listens carefully to the teacher's lesson.
why: 认真 is the manner of the verb 听 that follows, so 地. 得 only goes after a verb, and 认真 is not the main verb here.

q: 学生们安静___坐在教室里。
zh: 学生们安静地坐在教室里。
py: xué sheng men ān jìng de zuò zài jiào shì lǐ
en: The students sat quietly in the classroom.
why: 安静 tells how they sat and comes before the verb 坐, so 地. 得 would belong after a verb.

q: 小王仔细___检查了每一份文件。
zh: 小王仔细地检查了每一份文件。
py: xiǎo wáng zǐ xì de jiǎn chá le měi yī fèn wén jiàn
en: Xiao Wang carefully checked every document.
why: 仔细 is the manner of the action 检查 which follows, so 地. 得 would need a verb before the gap.

q: 经理耐心___回答了客户的问题。
zh: 经理耐心地回答了客户的问题。
py: jīng lǐ nài xīn de huí dá le kè hù de wèn tí
en: The manager patiently answered the client's questions.
why: 耐心 describes how the manager answered, and the verb 回答 comes right after the gap, so 地. 得 is wrong because no verb comes before it.

q: 为了准备考试，她每天都努力___复习到很晚。
zh: 为了准备考试，她每天都努力地复习到很晚。
py: wèi le zhǔn bèi kǎo shì tā měi tiān dōu nǔ lì de fù xí dào hěn wǎn
en: To prepare for the exam, she studies hard every day until late.
why: 努力 describes the manner of 复习, which follows the gap, so 地. 得 would need a verb before 努力 in a pattern like 学得很努力.

q: 开会的时候，大家都专心___听经理介绍新的计划。
zh: 开会的时候，大家都专心地听经理介绍新的计划。
py: kāi huì de shí hou dà jiā dōu zhuān xīn de tīng jīng lǐ jiè shào xīn de jì huà
en: During the meeting, everyone listened attentively as the manager introduced the new plan.
why: 专心 is how everyone listened and comes directly before the verb 听, so 地. 得 would have to follow the verb 听.

q: 你慢慢___说，我听得懂。
zh: 你慢慢地说，我听得懂。
py: nǐ màn màn de shuō wǒ tīng de dǒng
en: Say it slowly; I can understand.
why: 慢慢 is a doubled adjective before the verb 说, so 地. The doubling does not change the rule: before a verb it is 地, not 得.

q: 她有一双大大___眼睛。
zh: 她有一双大大的眼睛。
py: tā yǒu yī shuāng dà dà de yǎn jing
en: She has a pair of big eyes.
why: 大大 is a doubled adjective but it describes the noun 眼睛, so 的. Doubling does not turn it into 地.

q: 他轻轻___关上了办公室的门。
zh: 他轻轻地关上了办公室的门。
py: tā qīng qīng de guān shàng le bàn gōng shì de mén
en: He closed the office door gently.
why: 轻轻 is the manner of 关上 which comes next, so 地. 得 would require a verb before 轻轻.

q: 你把教室打扫___干干净净，老师会高兴的。
zh: 你把教室打扫得干干净净，老师会高兴的。
py: nǐ bǎ jiào shì dǎ sǎo de gān gān jìng jìng lǎo shī huì gāo xìng de
en: Clean the classroom spotless and the teacher will be pleased.
why: 干干净净 is a doubled adjective but it is the result after the verb 打扫, so 得. The doubled form does not choose 地 here.

q: 她高高兴兴___去公司上班了。
zh: 她高高兴兴地去公司上班了。
py: tā gāo gāo xìng xìng de qù gōng sī shàng bān le
en: She went to work happily.
why: 高高兴兴 describes how she went and comes before the verb 去, so 地. 得 needs a verb right before it, which is missing.

q: 小李把桌子擦___干干净净。
zh: 小李把桌子擦得干干净净。
py: xiǎo lǐ bǎ zhuō zi cā de gān gān jìng jìng
en: Xiao Li wiped the table spotlessly clean.
why: 干干净净 follows the verb 擦 and states the resulting condition, so 得. 地 goes before verbs, and no noun follows for 的.

q: 他把报告整整齐齐___放在经理的桌子上。
zh: 他把报告整整齐齐地放在经理的桌子上。
py: tā bǎ bào gào zhěng zhěng qí qí de fàng zài jīng lǐ de zhuō zi shàng
en: He placed the report neatly on the manager's desk.
why: 整整齐齐 is placed before the verb 放 and tells how the report was put down, so 地. 得 would only work if the doubled adjective came after 放.

q: 桌子上放着一杯热热___咖啡，是同事刚给我倒的。
zh: 桌子上放着一杯热热的咖啡，是同事刚给我倒的。
py: zhuō zi shàng fàng zhe yī bēi rè rè de kā fēi shì tóng shì gāng gěi wǒ dào de
en: There's a cup of hot coffee on the desk that a colleague just poured for me.
why: 热热 describes the noun 咖啡, so 的, even though it is doubled. 得 and 地 both need a verb beside them.

q: 他是一个很努力___学生。
zh: 他是一个很努力的学生。
py: tā shì yī gè hěn nǔ lì de xué sheng
en: He is a very hardworking student.
why: The noun 学生 follows the gap, so 的. The same word 努力 would take 地 before a verb.

q: 他学___很认真。
zh: 他学得很认真。
py: tā xué de hěn rèn zhēn
en: He studies very conscientiously.
why: 很认真 judges how he studies and comes after the verb 学, so 得. The same word before a noun would be 认真的.

q: 她每天认真___做作业。
zh: 她每天认真地做作业。
py: tā měi tiān rèn zhēn de zuò zuò yè
en: She does her homework carefully every day.
why: 认真 comes before the verb 做 and gives its manner, so 地. After a verb it would be 得, and before a noun 的.

q: 小王的字写___很清楚，不用再抄一遍。
zh: 小王的字写得很清楚，不用再抄一遍。
py: xiǎo wáng de zì xiě de hěn qīng chu bù yòng zài chāo yī biàn
en: Xiao Wang's writing is very clear; there's no need to copy it again.
why: 很清楚 grades how the characters are written, and follows the verb 写, so 得. 地 would put 清楚 before the verb.

q: 请你清楚___告诉我你的想法。
zh: 请你清楚地告诉我你的想法。
py: qǐng nǐ qīng chu de gào sù wǒ nǐ de xiǎng fǎ
en: Please tell me your thoughts clearly.
why: 清楚 is the manner of 告诉 and stands before it, so 地. 得 would require the adjective to come after the verb.

q: 她的英语说___很流利。
zh: 她的英语说得很流利。
py: tā de yīng yǔ shuō de hěn liú lì
en: She speaks English very fluently.
why: The object 英语 is fronted, so 说 is directly followed by 得 and the judgement 很流利. 的 would need a noun after it.

q: 这是一份写得很清楚___报告，大家都看得懂。
zh: 这是一份写得很清楚的报告，大家都看得懂。
py: zhè shì yī fèn xiě de hěn qīng chu de bào gào dà jiā dōu kàn de dǒng
en: This is a clearly written report that everyone can understand.
why: 写得很清楚 is a whole phrase describing the noun 报告, so the link is 的. The earlier 得 in 写得 does not carry over to this gap.

q: 那位老师用流利___汉语给我们讲了一个故事。
zh: 那位老师用流利的汉语给我们讲了一个故事。
py: nà wèi lǎo shī yòng liú lì de hàn yǔ gěi wǒ men jiǎng le yī gè gù shi
en: That teacher told us a story in fluent Chinese.
why: 流利 describes the noun 汉语, so 的. The same word is 地 before a verb (流利地说) and 得 after one (说得流利).

q: 他把这个问题仔细___想了一遍，才回答经理。
zh: 他把这个问题仔细地想了一遍，才回答经理。
py: tā bǎ zhè ge wèn tí zǐ xì de xiǎng le yī biàn cái huí dá jīng lǐ
en: He thought the question over carefully before answering the manager.
why: 仔细 comes before the verb 想 and gives its manner, so 地. 得 would need 仔细 to follow a verb.

zh: 我哥哥开车开得很慢
py: wǒ gē ge kāi chē kāi de hěn màn
en: My older brother drives slowly.
why: With an object 车, the verb 开 is repeated and 得 is attached to the second one. The judgement 很慢 comes last.

zh: 小李昨天走得很晚
py: xiǎo lǐ zuó tiān zǒu de hěn wǎn
en: Xiao Li left very late yesterday.
why: 得 stays attached to the verb and the judgement follows it. The time word may sit before or after the subject.

zh: 孩子们高兴地跑出了教室
py: hái zi men gāo xìng de pǎo chū le jiào shì
en: The children ran happily out of the classroom.
why: 高兴地 is the manner of the action and goes right before the verb 跑出了, after the subject. It cannot follow the verb.

zh: 我听得懂他说的话
py: wǒ tīng de dǒng tā shuō de huà
en: I can understand what he says.
why: 得 sits between the verb 听 and the result word 懂 to mean 'can'. The object 他说的话 can also be fronted as the topic.

zh: 同事们热情地欢迎新来的经理
py: tóng shì men rè qíng de huān yíng xīn lái de jīng lǐ
en: The colleagues warmly welcomed the new manager.
why: 热情地 describes how they welcomed and sits before the verb 欢迎. 新来的 is a clause + 的 and must stay in front of the noun 经理.

s: 老师写汉字得很漂亮。
s_py: lǎo shī xiě hàn zì de hěn piào liang
zh: 老师写汉字写得很漂亮。
py: lǎo shī xiě hàn zì xiě de hěn piào liang
en: The teacher writes Chinese characters beautifully.
why: 得 must follow the verb, not the object 汉字. Repeat the verb: 写汉字写得很漂亮.

s: 我哥哥踢足球得很好。
s_py: wǒ gē ge tī zú qiú de hěn hǎo
zh: 我哥哥踢足球踢得很好。
py: wǒ gē ge tī zú qiú tī de hěn hǎo
en: My older brother plays football very well.
why: 踢足球 has an object, so the verb 踢 must be repeated before 得. 得 cannot attach to the object 足球.

s: 他汉语说得很好。
s_py: tā hàn yǔ shuō de hěn hǎo
zh: 他汉语说得很好。
py: tā hàn yǔ shuō de hěn hǎo
en: He speaks Chinese very well.
why: Fronting the object 汉语 lets 得 follow 说 directly, so no repeated verb is needed. It looks incomplete but is a correct pattern.

s: 弟弟今天起得很早。
s_py: dì di jīn tiān qǐ de hěn zǎo
zh: 弟弟今天起得很早。
py: dì di jīn tiān qǐ de hěn zǎo
en: My younger brother got up very early today.
why: 起 is directly followed by 得 and the judgement 很早. This is the right pattern even for a past event; no 了 is needed.

s: 我昨天不睡得好。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān bù shuì de hǎo
zh: 我昨天睡得不好。
py: wǒ zuó tiān shuì de bù hǎo
en: I didn't sleep well yesterday.
why: With 得 the negative goes on the judgement, after 得: 睡得不好. Putting 不 before the verb is wrong.

s: 我不听得懂老师说的话。
s_py: wǒ bù tīng de dǒng lǎo shī shuō de huà
zh: 我听不懂老师说的话。
py: wǒ tīng bù dǒng lǎo shī shuō de huà
en: I can't understand what the teacher says.
why: The negative of 听得懂 replaces 得 with 不: 听不懂. 不 before the verb is wrong.

s: 黑板上的字太小了，我看不清楚。
s_py: hēi bǎn shàng de zì tài xiǎo le wǒ kàn bù qīng chu
zh: 黑板上的字太小了，我看不清楚。
py: hēi bǎn shàng de zì tài xiǎo le wǒ kàn bù qīng chu
en: The characters on the blackboard are too small; I can't see them clearly.
why: The 'cannot' form swaps 得 for 不: 看不清楚. This is correct; no other 不 is needed.

s: 他的话我听得不懂。
s_py: tā de huà wǒ tīng de bù dǒng
zh: 他的话我听不懂。
py: tā de huà wǒ tīng bù dǒng
en: I can't understand what he says.
why: To say 'cannot understand' you replace 得 with 不: 听不懂. 听得不懂 mixes the two patterns and is wrong.

s: 我累地不想说话。
s_py: wǒ lèi de bù xiǎng shuō huà
zh: 我累得不想说话。
py: wǒ lèi de bù xiǎng shuō huà
en: I'm so tired I don't want to talk.
why: 累 + 得 + result clause means 'so tired that ...'. 地 would make being tired a manner of an action, which it cannot be.

s: 她高兴得一晚上都没有睡着。
s_py: tā gāo xìng de yī wǎn shang dōu méi yǒu shuì zháo
zh: 她高兴得一晚上都没有睡着。
py: tā gāo xìng de yī wǎn shang dōu méi yǒu shuì zháo
en: She was so happy that she didn't sleep all night.
why: 高兴 + 得 + result clause is the 'so ... that ...' pattern. Not sleeping is the result of being happy, so 得 is right.

s: 她买了一件漂亮地衣服。
s_py: tā mǎi le yī jiàn piào liang de yī fu
zh: 她买了一件漂亮的衣服。
py: tā mǎi le yī jiàn piào liang de yī fu
en: She bought a pretty piece of clothing.
why: 漂亮 describes the noun 衣服, so 的. 地 only goes before a verb.

s: 这是一个很有意思地故事。
s_py: zhè shì yī gè hěn yǒu yì si de gù shi
zh: 这是一个很有意思的故事。
py: zhè shì yī gè hěn yǒu yì si de gù shi
en: This is a very interesting story.
why: 很有意思 describes the noun 故事, so 的. 地 is wrong before a noun.

s: 这是妈妈做得菜。
s_py: zhè shì mā ma zuò de cài
zh: 这是妈妈做的菜。
py: zhè shì mā ma zuò de cài
en: This is the food Mum made.
why: 妈妈做 is a clause that describes the noun 菜, so it takes 的. 得 needs a judgement or result after it, not a noun.

s: 老师昨天讲的课，我都听懂了。
s_py: lǎo shī zuó tiān jiǎng de kè wǒ dōu tīng dǒng le
zh: 老师昨天讲的课，我都听懂了。
py: lǎo shī zuó tiān jiǎng de kè wǒ dōu tīng dǒng le
en: I understood all of the lesson the teacher gave yesterday.
why: 讲的课 is verb + 的 + noun: the clause describes the lesson. It looks like it needs 得, but a noun follows the gap, not a judgement.

s: 在门口等你得那个人是我的同事。
s_py: zài mén kǒu děng nǐ de nà ge rén shì wǒ de tóng shì
zh: 在门口等你的那个人是我的同事。
py: zài mén kǒu děng nǐ de nà ge rén shì wǒ de tóng shì
en: The person waiting for you at the door is my colleague.
why: 在门口等你 describes the person 那个人, so it needs 的. 得 cannot link a verb phrase to a noun.

s: 他认真地写作业。
s_py: tā rèn zhēn de xiě zuò yè
zh: 他认真地写作业。
py: tā rèn zhēn de xiě zuò yè
en: He does his homework carefully.
why: 认真 is the manner of 写 and sits before it, so 地 is right. The same adjective after the verb would need 得.

s: 经理仔细得检查了报告。
s_py: jīng lǐ zǐ xì de jiǎn chá le bào gào
zh: 经理仔细地检查了报告。
py: jīng lǐ zǐ xì de jiǎn chá le bào gào
en: The manager checked the report carefully.
why: 仔细 is the manner of 检查 and comes before the verb, so 地. 得 only goes after a verb or adjective.

s: 她把房间打扫得干干净净。
s_py: tā bǎ fáng jiān dǎ sǎo de gān gān jìng jìng
zh: 她把房间打扫得干干净净。
py: tā bǎ fáng jiān dǎ sǎo de gān gān jìng jìng
en: She cleaned the room spotless.
why: 干干净净 comes after the verb 打扫 and describes the result, so 得. A doubled adjective after a verb is still 得, not 地.

s: 你慢慢得说。
s_py: nǐ màn màn de shuō
zh: 你慢慢地说。
py: nǐ màn màn de shuō
en: Say it slowly.
why: 慢慢 sits before the verb 说 and gives its manner, so 地. 得 would need a verb before it.

s: 他有一双大大的眼睛，笑起来特别可爱。
s_py: tā yǒu yī shuāng dà dà de yǎn jing xiào qǐ lái tè bié kě ài
zh: 他有一双大大的眼睛，笑起来特别可爱。
py: tā yǒu yī shuāng dà dà de yǎn jing xiào qǐ lái tè bié kě ài
en: He has big eyes and looks especially cute when he smiles.
why: 大大 is doubled, but it describes the noun 眼睛, so 的 is correct. Doubling does not turn it into 地.

s: 她唱歌地很好。
s_py: tā chàng gē de hěn hǎo
zh: 她唱歌唱得很好。
py: tā chàng gē chàng de hěn hǎo
en: She sings well.
why: 'Sings well' is a judgement on the singing: repeat 唱 and use 得. 地 cannot follow an object.

s: 同学们学得很认真。
s_py: tóng xué men xué de hěn rèn zhēn
zh: 同学们学得很认真。
py: tóng xué men xué de hěn rèn zhēn
en: The students study very conscientiously.
why: 很认真 judges how they study and follows the verb 学, so 得. The same word before a verb would take 地.

s: 他每天认真得做作业，成绩一直很好。
s_py: tā měi tiān rèn zhēn de zuò zuò yè chéng jì yī zhí hěn hǎo
zh: 他每天认真地做作业，成绩一直很好。
py: tā měi tiān rèn zhēn de zuò zuò yè chéng jì yī zhí hěn hǎo
en: He does his homework carefully every day, and his grades have always been good.
why: 认真 comes before the verb 做 and describes its manner, so 地. 得 would need the adjective to follow a verb.

s: 他很快地吃完了早饭，就去上班了。
s_py: tā hěn kuài de chī wán le zǎo fàn jiù qù shàng bān le
zh: 他很快地吃完了早饭，就去上班了。
py: tā hěn kuài de chī wán le zǎo fàn jiù qù shàng bān le
en: He finished breakfast quickly and then went to work.
why: 很快 describes the manner of this one action and stands before the verb 吃完, so 地. It looks wrong next to 吃得很快, but both are correct.

s: 上次的会议经理不讲得太详细，我们还有很多问题。
s_py: shàng cì de huì yì jīng lǐ bù jiǎng de tài xiáng xì wǒ men hái yǒu hěn duō wèn tí
zh: 上次的会议经理讲得不太详细，我们还有很多问题。
py: shàng cì de huì yì jīng lǐ jiǎng de bù tài xiáng xì wǒ men hái yǒu hěn duō wèn tí
en: In the last meeting the manager wasn't very detailed, and we still have many questions.
why: With 得 the negative goes on the judgement: 讲得不太详细. Putting 不 before the verb is wrong.
